cases.name: unparseable-stdin-noop
cases._branch: json.load(sys.stdin) raises -> sys.exit(0). stdin omitted so the harness attaches /dev/null; the reader sees EOF.

cases.name: non-bash-tool-noop
cases._branch: tool_name != "Bash" -> sys.exit(0). Payload otherwise names a real .typ so only the tool-name gate can stop it.

cases.name: bash-command-does-not-match-trigger
cases._branch: TRIGGER_RE.search(command) is None -> sys.exit(0). Deliberate near-miss: a bare `typst compile` of an existing .typ. Only `tinymist compile` may fire; a port that loosens the regex to `compile .*\.typ` breaks here.

cases.name: trigger-matches-but-target-not-on-disk
cases._branch: os.path.exists(cwd/target) is False -> sys.exit(0). The generated/temp-target skip: command matches TRIGGER_RE, capture group is `build/generated.typ`, which the fixture does not create.

cases.name: trigger-matches-flat-target-exists
cases._branch: Deepest externally reachable branch: regex matched, `slides.typ` exists in cwd, so control reaches find_scripts_dir(). With no teaching/teaching plugin installed the lookup returns None -> sys.exit(0), no stdout, and crucially NO cwd/output/ directory and no typst/uv subprocess. Pins that the port stops before the side-effecting stage.

tool_input.description: Compile the deck for visual verification

cases.name: trigger-matches-subdir-target-exists
cases._branch: Same terminal branch as above but through a nested path (`presentation/slides.typ`), pinning that the capture group is used verbatim and joined against cwd rather than basenamed or forced under a literal `slides/` directory.
